newsitem.title: USA: Senate committee approves Garvey for FAA head.
newsitem.headline: Senate committee approves Garvey for FAA head.

text.p: The Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation Wednesday unanimously approved the nomination of Jane Garvey to head the Federal Aviation Administration.
Garvey's nomination will now be considered before the full Senate.
Garvey is a former director of Boston's Logan International Airport and is the current acting head of the Federal Highway Administration.

"Jane Garvey is an outstanding choice to lead the FAA into the twenty-first century," Senator John Kerry, a Democrat from Massachussetts, said. "I hope the Senate will now move quickly to get Jane on the job full-time as soon as possible."
President Clinton nominated Garvey June 11 to replace David Hinson, who left the FAA in November after three years at the post.
